URL: https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/about-us/news-and-media/media-centre/weather-and-climate-news/2026/heatwave-continues-as-uk-records-unprecedented-run-of-35c-days
(WebFetch content — Met Office media-centre reporting language, late July 2026)
Met Office: UK has recorded a record EIGHT days exceeding 34C this year, surpassing 1976 and 2020. First year in UK records with 35C+ in May, June AND July.
Dr Amy Doherty, Met Office Science Manager: "This year has already seen a number of remarkable temperature milestones. Not only have we now recorded a record eight days with temperatures exceeding 34C, surpassing the previous record held by 1976 and 2020..."
David Hayter, Met Office Deputy Chief Forecaster: "Areas of central and southern England and Wales are expected to see several more consecutive days of temperatures above 30C."
Amber and yellow heat-health alerts in place across England; heat expected to persist and shift westward.

URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_Kingdom_heatwaves
UKHSA (with Met Office) issued amber heat-health alert on 27 July for East Midlands, East of England, London and South East — in force 9am Wed 29 July to 9am Thu 30 July. Yellow alerts for South West, West Midlands, Yorkshire & the Humber. Fourth heatwave of summer began 28 July; temperatures expected to reach mid-30s later in the week. Under amber alert UKHSA warns significant impacts "likely." Hosepipe bans already affecting ~23m customers; drought declared across large parts of Wales.
(NB: BBC reported this heatwave reached 34.7C — https://feeds.bbci.co.uk/news/articles/crmv8x74ky9o ; a fresh separately-confirmed 28-July peak figure was not located.)
